paper.title: Machin's arctangent formula for pi (1706) and Stormer's four-term formula (1896), as used for hand and machine computation of pi digits
paper.venue: Machin: in W. Jones, Synopsis Palmariorum Matheseos (1706); Stormer: Archiv for Mathematik og Naturvidenskab 19 (1896)

program.how: written for ounce-core from the two arctangent identities and the Gregory series atan(1/x) = sum (-1)^k / ((2k+1) x^(2k+1)); own fixed-point decimal arithmetic (base 10^9 limbs, small-integer division, add, subtract); no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: Machin's formula pi/4 = 4 atan(1/5) - atan(1/239) yields 10000 digits of pi (the 3 and 9999 decimals), all equal to the digits listed in OEIS A000796
Stormer's formula pi/4 = 44 atan(1/57) + 7 atan(1/239) - 12 atan(1/682) + 24 atan(1/12943) yields the same 10000 digits

expected_values_source.what: the decimal digits of pi (sequence A000796), first 10000 digits, copied as data. The two original publications were not fetched; the formulas are classical identities, the check shows that they give these digits.
expected_values_source.note: the digit list and the program are independent of each other, so agreement over 10000 digits for two different formulas confirms both

negative_control: built with -DMACHIN_C5=3 (3 instead of 4 as the coefficient of atan(1/5)), Machin's formula yields 2352010414.. and differs at digit 1 and the program exits 1
not_checked: digits beyond 10000, and Shanks' 1873 computation (707 places, of which only the first 527 are correct) which was not fetched
that the identities hold as identities (only that they give these 10000 digits)
other Machin-like formulas (Takano, Gauss, Euler's atan form) and FFT-based or Chudnovsky methods
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, reproduces the first 10000 digits of pi from two arctangent formulas. It does not show anything about larger digit counts.
